problem: Object-goal navigation methods relying on heuristic distances, graph structures or learned priors generalize poorly to unseen scenes and objects, while LLM-as-planner/agent approaches are costly, unstable under prompt paraphrasing, and lack experience specific to the target household distribution.
motivation: Efficient ObjectNav needs object-object semantic relationships that both generalize (LLM commonsense) and fit the target domain (training experience). Directly querying LLMs at every step is expensive and yields inconsistent scores, so a cheap numeric affinity plugin that works with existing policies is desirable.
key_idea: Fuse a learned experiential affinity (scaled dot-product on text embeddings) with an LLM-derived binary relevance affinity via a context-dependent gate, and use the fused scores to activate semantic-map channels or graph nodes of any downstream navigation policy.
insight: LLM knowledge is used only as binary relevance (not exact scores) to avoid prompt instability, and pre-computed once so there is no per-step LLM cost. The submodule ablation (HOZ on SAVN-NAV) shows each module gives only small gains alone (SR 72.40 with G.A., 72.51 with E.A. vs 72.20 baseline) while the full fusion gives the best (73.12), i.e. the two sources are complementary. Out-of-domain qualitative tests show that G.A. fixes implausible placement of unseen objects (e.g. can opener near bathtub).
method: Experiential Affinities Module: encodes category names with paraphrase-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d), applies learned W_q/W_k, and computes softmax scaled dot-product scores between the target and every map object, co-trained with the downstream policy.
Generalized Affinities Module: GPT-4 gives a binary relevance S(o_i,target) per object (stored offline); the weights are normalized uniformly over relevant objects.

Dynamic Fusion Module: two 2-layer MLPs on temporal context (RNN hidden state or trajectory/explored regions) plus environment features output the guidance ratio gamma; A_F = gamma*A_G + (1-gamma)*A_E.
Map-based integration: scale each semantic map channel by its fused affinity score (element-wise) to bias the search toward relevant categories.
Graph-based integration: average the affinity of objects in each node and multiply it with the node embedding to activate relevant nodes.
Two-stage training: first co-train the E.A. module with the downstream policy, then freeze both and train only the fusion layer with G.A. added.
LOAT-P: FILM with a fine-tuned DINO segmenter and Prompter-style exploration, plus LOAT semantic map activation, for ALFRED.

setting.backbone: Downstream policies (FILM/Prompter-based LOAT-P, HOZ+A3C, PEANUT) with MiniLM text encoder and GPT-4 (offline relevance); fine-tuned DINO segmenter for ALFRED
setting.training_data: Each downstream benchmark's own training data (ALFRED, SAVN-NAV in AI2-THOR, Habitat ObjectNav); GPT-4 relevance labels; no extra web data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, with semantic maps or topological graphs built from detected objects
setting.action_space: Downstream policy actions (discrete low-level actions / waypoints on map; HOZ discrete actions in AI2-THOR)

results: LOAT-P sets SOTA on ALFRED, with test-unseen SR 54.22 vs 43.69 for CAPEAM and 42.64 for Prompter. LOAT gives consistent gains as a plugin: HOZ SR 72.20→73.12 on SAVN-NAV, PEANUT SR 0.55→0.63 on Habitat, and Prompter/FILM on ALFRED valid splits. Real-robot LoCoBot trials found all five target categories without extra training.
limitations: Gains on SAVN-NAV are small (<1 point) and no variance or significance reported; the ALFRED gain is confounded by DINO and Prompter changes
Depends on the fixed closed category set of the semantic map; extending to open-vocabulary is unresolved
Real-world validation is small (5 categories, 3 trials per scene, 2 scenes) and the out-of-domain evaluation is qualitative
